title: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis: a prognostic and therapeutic study
authors: Seidowsky A, Nseir S, Houdret N, Fourrier F
followUp: intensive care admission to discharge or death; ten-year retrospective period
population: Patients admitted to two intensive care units (50 beds) of a French university hospital with metformin-associated lactic acidosis: 13 voluntary intoxications and 29 incidental overdoses
funder: Not stated in the published abstract. The full text is behind a subscription, the article is absent from PubMed Central and no repository copy is indexed, so the funding statement could not be read and the class is undetermined.
result: Results read from the published abstract. Of 42 patients, 74% were in acute renal failure and needed haemodialysis. No death occurred among the 13 patients with intentional overdose, against 48.3% mortality among the 29 with incidental overdose. Factors significantly associated with mortality were the logistic organ dysfunction system score, pH, plasma lactate and prothrombin activity; by multivariate analysis a prothrombin activity below 50% was the only independent predictor of death (relative risk 59.8, confidence limits 6.3 to 568, p < 0.0001). Sequential metformin levels during haemodialysis followed a bicompartmental elimination pattern, and a cumulative dialysis duration of 15 hours returned metformin to the therapeutic range. The authors describe metformin-associated lactic acidosis as usually arising when a precipitating disease causes acute renal failure and an incidental overdose.
